bolinas-cultist.intro: Afternoon. Good day for a walk. The geese usually come in around four. I count them from the porch. Most days I get the same number.

choices.label: What happens when the count is off?
choices.receipt: I count again. Last Tuesday, eleven went out and twelve came back. The extra one looked right at my window. Wait. Who told you to ask about the count? I have nothing to tell you.

choices.label: Is that your cottage?
choices.receipt: Has been for years. The geese used to walk straight past it. Lately one stops at the gate, right where you’re standing. Did somebody send you to ask about the house? I have nothing to tell you.

choices.label: What does a share get me?
choices.receipt: A small stake in the startup. You don’t have to come to stand-up meetings for it. If you decide to sell, take the share to the Venture Exchange and ask what they’re paying that day.

choices.label: What kind of shares do you buy?
choices.receipt: Ordinary startup shares. I deal with people who want to sell one or two at a time. Public growth shares go through the stockbroker. Around here the paperwork is short enough that I can get back to my coffee while it’s still hot.

coffee-stall-vendor.intro: Fresh coffee, brewed right here. Want a cup?

hardware-clerk.intro: Need a little leverage? I carry steel crowbars.

rich-table-chef.intro: If you find any fresh uni along the coast, I’ll buy it from you for the kitchen.

choices.label: Do you get many hikers here?
choices.receipt: A few come up from the lake and a few are waiting for the road to clear. You can usually tell which ones have been up here before. They stop for a sandwich before they ask whether the weather will hold.

choices.label: What kind of work would I do?
What does the phone do?
choices.receipt: Keep it equipped and some of your earnings get a lift. The idea was to let you do a little business wherever you happen to be. We had rather more success than we expected getting people to keep it in their hand.

choices.label: Is there a catch?
choices.receipt: I find myself looking at the screen before I remember why I took it out. After a while, doomscrolling costs hitpoints. You can put the phone away from your character controls and bring it out again whenever you like.

choices.label: Why is the campus round?
choices.receipt: I used to get to the end of a hallway and turn back toward my desk. Here I keep walking. You get a good look at the courtyard that way, if you remember to look up.

choices.label: When should I put the phone away?
choices.receipt: If you’re out exploring and find yourself watching the screen more than the path, that’s a good time. The earnings boost needs the phone equipped. Putting it away also pauses the hitpoint drain from doomscrolling.

choices.label: Why is the campus round?
choices.receipt: I used to get to the end of a hallway and turn back toward my desk. Here I keep walking. You get a good look at the courtyard that way, if you remember to look up.

choices.label: Who collects the fares?
choices.receipt: You do. The car handles the driving and completed fares go into your purse. You’re buying a car to work in the fleet. If you just want a ride across town, you can call a Waymo from your travel controls.

choices.label: Where does it go between fares?
choices.receipt: Dispatch sends the car wherever there’s someone to pick up. I don’t keep an itinerary at the desk. Last time I tried, a passenger asked for a scenic route and the whole page was out of date by lunch.

choices.label: What am I buying?
choices.receipt: Growth equity is a stake in a company that’s moved past the early startup stage. The stake is private when you buy it here, so there’s no public price to check yet. If you’ve bought little startup shares elsewhere, those are a different thing.

choices.label: What does taking it public mean?
choices.receipt: The stockbroker in Times Square can put the stake on the public market. After that, the quote moves with what buyers are willing to pay. People come up here asking what they’ll make on the sale. I can tell them what the shares cost today. The rest is up to the market.

choices.label: How should I read the quote?
choices.receipt: It tells you what the market is offering for the shares right now. There’s a separate listing fee when you first go public, and you can ask me to sell while the shares are trading. I can read out today’s price. I can’t tell you where it will go.

choices.receipt: The town’s fine. I see the same neighbors every morning, even when the fog is thick enough that we have to recognize each other by the shopping bags. The beach is usually the quietest place once the wind drops.

choices.label: What’s good today?
choices.receipt: Whatever the delivery truck can get down the coast road. This morning that meant bread, apples, and six crates of something I was assured would sell better once I’d tried it.

world.interactions.interactCitizen.node-.intro: Morning. Come in out of the fog. It’s an early one today. I had to walk halfway down the street to see whether I’d opened the shop sign.

choices.receipt: I like it when the beach is quiet enough to hear the water pull back over the stones. Ask someone at the shop when the fog came in and you’ll get a more reliable answer than you will from me.

choices.label: What are you watching for?
choices.receipt: Give it a minute and watch where the water starts to fold. The first wave can make the whole set look promising. I’ve done enough paddling for one morning to wait and see the second.

world.interactions.interactCitizen.node-.intro: Hey. I’m waiting to see what the wind does. Somebody said the best wave of the month came in yesterday. Funny how often that happens on the day I’m working.

actor:twitter-bottle-worker.dialogue-1.speech: One envelope in, one bottle out. Please do not tap the backend.

choices.label: What makes a good report?
choices.receipt: A place, a time, and what you saw with your own eyes. Two people can disagree about what caused something and still give me a good record of what happened. The window is open when you have something to bring by.

choices.label: Ask about the office
choices.receipt: Permits, certificates, authorizations. Come back when you have an activity that needs permitting.

salt-mail.saltClerkDialogue.node-13:intr.v0: City Hall issues a permit for nearly everything. Sometimes the category has to be invented first.

choices.label: What do you do out here?
choices.receipt: The people inside design the experiments. My job is to work out how they behave in fresh air, with mud underfoot and something leaning against the fence. That last part rarely makes it onto the slides.

poster-reply.intro: Hang on. Someone is wrong on the internet, and I’ve just spent ten minutes finding a much nicer way to say so. Welcome to Posting HQ. Most of us meant to leave five minutes ago.

choices.label: What are you posting about?
choices.receipt: A man said nobody walks anywhere in San Francisco. I walked here to write a reply. By the time I’d finished, he’d changed the subject to parking, so I think we both learned something.

choices.label: Is it always this busy?
choices.receipt: It gets quiet around lunch. You can hear the chairs creak while everyone tries to think of a good opening line. Then somebody posts a photograph of a sandwich and we remember how to be neighbors.
